articles.excerpt: Abstract:Agents that investigate and decide on enterprise security reason over a machine-readable view of the environment: its assets, identities, configurations, relations, and findings. articles.title: An Exploration of Attacks on AI Agent Systems
articles.excerpt: Abstract:As autonomous AI agents become more integrated into sensitive domains, it is crucial that single and multi-agent AI systems are secured. While our tests mostly highlight key vulnerabilities in single-agent systems, we also extend these attacks to multi-agent frameworks, investigating how weaknesses can propagate across agents. Our findings emphasize the need for more robust defenses as AI agents become more commonly embedded in real-world workflows.

articles.excerpt: Abstract:Memory-dependent manipulation requires a policy to track execution state and recover visual evidence that is no longer observable. articles.title: Beyond Actions: Learning Future Operation Targets for Vision-Language-Action Models
articles.excerpt: Abstract:Actions specify what a robot should execute, but do not describe what those commands will achieve. articles.title: ReAT: Residual Action Tokenization for Autoregressive Robot Policies
articles.excerpt: Abstract:Autoregressive robot policies rely on action tokenizers to convert continuous action chunks into compact sequences of discrete prediction targets. Existing tokenizers can reconstruct action chunks from discrete codes, but often leave implicit what each individual token contributes to the reconstructed action. We introduce Residual Action Tokenization (ReAT), which gives each token an explicit role in refining the current action reconstruction. It uses the decoded reconstruction as feedback to construct the next token from the remaining action error. This closes the loop between encoding and decoding, making each new token responsive to the errors left by the actual decoded prefix. articles.excerpt: Abstract:People often learn how an unfamiliar object moves through a small exploratory push, using its response to guide their next motion. articles.excerpt: Abstract:Action-chunking policies predict future controls but execute only a prefix before replanning. How should a fixed action-token budget be organized to support execution? articles.excerpt: Abstract:Humanoid and service robots operating in clut- tered human environments may encounter motion planning problems that are infeasible when all surrounding objects are treated as fixed obstacles. articles.excerpt: Abstract:Embodied coding agents construct robot policies from natural-language instructions by generating executable programs and refining them from execution feedback. articles.excerpt: Abstract:Scaling generalist robotic policies is limited by the high cost of collecting embodied interaction data. articles.title: AlphaNIST: Emergent Assembly Skills from Binary Task Rewards
articles.excerpt: Abstract:The NIST Assembly Task Board #1 remains a challenging benchmark for learning-based methods in robotic manipulation. articles.excerpt: Abstract:A useful language model should know when to answer and when to say "I don't know."
